title: Fear and suffering, Illness and boil, Both clinging and swamp, Are called sensual pleasures. There the ordinary person, Infatuated and clinging, Sees fear in clinging,…
content:
Fear and suffering,
Illness and boil,
Both clinging and swamp,
Are called sensual pleasures.
There the ordinary person,
Infatuated and clinging,
Sees fear in clinging,
The origin of birth and death.
Without clinging, liberated,
Birth and death are destroyed,
They attain security,
Pure bliss in this life,
Overcome fear and enmity,
All suffering is overcome.

title: - Friends, defilement is called defilement — what is the synonym for what is called defilement? - Friends, evil, unwholesome states, the domain of sensual…
content:
- Friends, defilement is called defilement — what is the synonym for what is called defilement?
- Friends, evil, unwholesome states, the domain of sensual desire, are the synonym for what is called defilement.

title: And, bhikkhus, what is the Noble Truth of Suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are…
content: And, bhikkhus, what is the Noble Truth of Suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; not getting what one wants is suffering; in short, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering.

title: Elder Valliya: The duties to be done with energy and diligence, The duties to be done for one who wishes to awaken — I will…
content:
Elder Valliya:

The duties to be done with energy and diligence,
The duties to be done for one who wishes to awaken —
I will do them all, I will not backslide.
See my diligence, my effort!

Please tell me the path entering the Deathless.
With silent meditation I have attained noble silence,
Like the Ganges River entering the great ocean.

title: - Just as, bhikkhus, this great earth were entirely covered with water, and a person throws a yoke with a single hole into it. An…
content: - Just as, bhikkhus, this great earth were entirely covered with water, and a person throws a yoke with a single hole into it. An east wind would carry it west, a west wind would carry it east, a north wind would carry it south, a south wind would carry it north. There is a blind turtle that surfaces once every hundred years. What do you think, bhikkhus, would that blind turtle, surfacing once every hundred years, put its neck into that yoke with a single hole?" - "It would be hard, Venerable Sir, for that blind turtle, surfacing once every hundred years, to put its neck into that yoke with a single hole!" - "It is just as hard, bhikkhus, to obtain human birth! It is just as hard, bhikkhus, for a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, to appear in the world! It is just as hard, bhikkhus, for the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata to shine in the world! But now, bhikkhus, you have obtained human birth, and a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, has appeared in the world, and the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines in the world. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

title: Bhikkhus, among whatever beings there are — whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed, whether having form or formless, whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient — the…
content: Bhikkhus, among whatever beings there are — whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed, whether having form or formless, whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient — the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One is declared the foremost among them. So too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, all are rooted in heedfulness, all converge on heedfulness, and heedfulness is declared the foremost among them.

title: Form, sound, odor, taste, touch, And all mind-objects, Desirable, lovely, agreeable — Thus they are called. Devas and humans Consider them delightful. Where they cease,…
content:
Form, sound, odor, taste, touch,
And all mind-objects,
Desirable, lovely, agreeable —
Thus they are called.

Devas and humans
Consider them delightful.
Where they cease,
Devas and humans see suffering.

The noble one sees happiness
When identity view ceases.
The noble one sees the opposite
Of all the world's views.

What people call happiness,
The noble one calls suffering.
What people call suffering,
The noble one knows as happiness.

Seeing the Dhamma hard to discern,
The ignorant are confused.
Darkness for the ignorant,
Blindness for those who do not see.

The good person with open eyes,
Sees clearly the light,
Lives near, knows clearly,
Skilled in the great Dhamma.

Overcome by the thirst for becoming,
Swept away by the stream of existence,
Controlled by Māra,
They do not awaken to this Dhamma.

Apart from the noble ones, no one
Awakens to this path,
The path to Nibbāna,
With right knowledge, free from taints.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple dwelling at home, with mind free from the stain of miserliness, gives generously, with open hand, delighting in relinquishment, ready…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple dwelling at home, with mind free from the stain of miserliness, gives generously, with open hand, delighting in relinquishment, ready to be asked, delighting in distributing gifts. This, bhikkhus, is called the wealth of giving.

title: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu reflects: 'Such is form, such is the arising of form, such is the passing away of form. Such is feeling, such is…
content: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu reflects: 'Such is form, such is the arising of form, such is the passing away of form. Such is feeling, such is the arising of feeling, such is the passing away of feeling. Such is perception, such is the arising of perception, such is the passing away of perception. Such are formations, such is the arising of formations, such is the passing away of formations. Such is consciousness, such is the arising of consciousness, such is the passing away of consciousness.' Thus he dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena internally; or he dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena externally; or he dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena both internally and externally. Or he dwells contemplating the nature of arising in phenomena; or he dwells contemplating the nature of passing away in phenomena; or he dwells contemplating the nature of both arising and passing away in phenomena. 'There are phenomena,' mindfulness is established in him to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. And he dwells independent, not clinging to anything in the world. Bhikkhus, that is how a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena as phenomena with respect to the five aggregates of clinging.

title: Here, Venerable Sir, I see bhikkhus living the holy life perfectly and purely for the whole of their life, until their last breath. Venerable Sir,…
content: Here, Venerable Sir, I see bhikkhus living the holy life perfectly and purely for the whole of their life, until their last breath. Venerable Sir, I do not see any other holy life elsewhere that is so perfect and pure. Venerable Sir, this is my conviction regarding the Blessed One: 'The Blessed One is perfectly enlightened; the Dhamma is well taught by the Blessed One; the Saṅgha of the Blessed One's disciples is well practiced and well trained.'
